public.title: Inorder Successor in BST
public.description: Given a valid BST with distinct values and a target value present in it, return the next greater value, or null if target is largest. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the first value is the root; each non-null node consumes the next two entries as left and right children. Null marks a missing child; trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no tree. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000, with at most 200 nodes.
hints: Search for the smallest BST value strictly greater than target.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Adapted from a standard algorithmic problem; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: When a node exceeds target, retain it and search left for a smaller successor; otherwise search right. O(height) time.
